questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose ULB and Brussels as my destination to get wiser on the EU because I want to use it later in my career. I did not think- and still do not believe - that there is a better place in the world to gain more knowledge about the EU than at the Heart of the Union. As mentioned in my application I wished to improve my French by living in a country with French as official language and furthermore take courses in French. Since I am dreaming of working with European politics, where French is the key word for communication, this part was an important motivation for my exchange due to career opportunities in the future. Mastering the French language with its sophisticated and difficult nuances requires an everyday life with the language, where it fills in everything from teaching to shopping trips, but also in relationships to new acquaintances. A stay in Brussels will and have allowed me to live the life of a true European citizen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great stay. But - many bureaucratic barriers from both host university and home university. It takes a bit of the joy out of the whole process. Everything else was fine - and ULB is excellent at European politics.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It has not exactly been easy. You are on your own and have to figure everything yourself. ULB has been good at sending out joint e-mails for all exchange students, but from the beginning I have been on my own. ULB has definitely been doing a better job than my home university (University of Copenhagen).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got 3 joint e-mails to all exchange students with informations and instructions. Furthermore, ULB hosted a meeting on how to apply for courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Okay. I contacted Hélène Seutin, that is the one person housing all the Danish Interns. I therefore stayed in a shared house with 6 other interns to 490 euro/month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easy to find a room in joint appartment in the city center. It's difficult to interact with international students if living in intern housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult, but of course successful in the end. It was unnecessarily cumbersome from start to finish as well as the entire process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You needed to apply for courses in Google Docs followed by a pink form and later it became available online. Registration was handled through UCPH which was fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can e-mail the coordinator or use office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted after the course catalogue was updated 2 weeks before the semester started. I think that was a little too late, since I already submitted my Learning Agreement at that time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. Things are going slowly in Belgium.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the EU courses were fantastic!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a few MA-courses that I found very appropriate in level. The rest were BA-courses, which I think were a bit boring and banal.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot of rote learning and lacked a little reflection and larger lines compared to what I am used to in Copenhagen. However, I think the MA-courses were really good at translating theory into practice with simulation games and assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Introduction to Political Science
2. Introduction to EU Politics
3. Histoire de l'epoque contemporaine
4. Institutions and political representation
5. European Integration and Public Policy
6. Vie politique en Belgique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Institutions and political representation: Gilles Piotters is a great teacher!
- European Integration and Public Policy: Mrs. Crepsy takes the theory and place it into reality. One of the best professors on EU-integration.
- Vie politique en Belgique: Great course if you want to know more about Belgian Politics

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was great

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sport, club for exchange students, trips etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The exchange student club was great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips around Belgium (get out of Brussels); Gent, Brugge, The Ardennes etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, however, things are somewhat less formal and tend to be a bit messy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet both international students and the Danish interns

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The garbage system and half solutions: Things are rarely followed to the door in Belgium if you do not push very hard.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Enjoying the weekend in peace and quiet. The shops, museums and so on are closed on Sundays, so Belgians get along with friends to relax and enjoy life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make use of the Danish network, but make sure not to stay in the closed Danish bubble alone.
2. Be sure to take EU-courses at ULB. They are extremely good at it. 
3. Speak French - take advantage of the fact that you are in a country where you can improve your French.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To learn about the European Union up close and have courses in French. It showed rapid progress.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Patience. Both with fellow students, professors and Belgians in general. There is a completely different pace and a more relaxed approach to things - regardless of their importance. As a Dane, it is a great contrast to experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
